full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J.:- This criminal appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 11. 03. 2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10817 or 2005 making the Rule absolute. 

 4. On receipt of the petition of complaint, the learned Magistrate. Sylhet sent the same to the CID, Sylhet Zone, with a direction to treat the same as first information report. Accordingly Kotwali Police Station Case No. 66 dated 25.04.2005 under section 467/109/471/420/406 was started. 

 5. The accused respondents appeared before the High Court Division on 09.07.2005 and were enlarged on ad-interim anticipatory bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7872 of 2 005. 

 7. By the impugned judgment and order the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and quashed the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 387 of 2005 arising out of Kotwali Police Station Case No. 66 dated 25.04.2005 and hence the appellant filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 197 of 2007 and leave was granted on the following submissions of Mr. Mahbuhey Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner: 

 "For that the High Court Division erred in holding that without filing a naraji petition a fresh petition of complaint does not lie and thereby erred in quashing the subsequent petition of complaint filed by the petitioner. For that the petitioner who is the complainant having stated that there is no reason to execute a deed of gift in favour of his daughter-in-law when her marital relationship with the complainant's son has severed for about one year prior to the alleged execution of the deed of gift, the High Court Division committed an error in quashing the proceeding without considering the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 For that the police having submitted final report against the accused in the earlier case without taking any steps for comparison of the thumb impression of the complainant petitioner with the thumb impression in the alleged deed of gift and being biased police having submitted final report in the earlier case, the High court Division erred in quashing the subsequent petition of complaint filed by the petitioner holding that the dispute between the parties is of civil nature." 

 8. Mr. Biswajit Deb Nath, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line the grounds upon which leave was granted. He also submitted that the High Court Division failed to notice that the case reported in 15 BLD (AD) 3 was distinguishable from the facts and circumstance of the present case and erred in not holding that the case reported in 6 DLR (AD) 279 and 36 DLR (AD) 58 is applicable in the instant case. 

 9. Mr. Zainul Abedin, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the case respondent Nos. 1 & 3 made submission in support of the judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

 12. In The case of Abdus Salam Vs. State 36 DLR (AD) 58, referred by the learned D.A.G this Division, upon meticulous consideration of decisions of the Indian Supreme Court and Pakistan Supreme Court, reaffirmed the principle of law that a fresh complaint may be entertained after dismissal of the previous one or after acceptance of the 'Final Report', on the same allegation, against the same person; but this power of the Magistrate is not unqualified, unrestricted or unbridled. This power is circumscribed by so many factors which may collectively be termed as "exceptional circumstances". Their Lordships went on to say that this power should be exercised when the previous order of dismissal is manifestly illegal or absurd or when fresh materials come forward which were not available when the previous complaint was considered. In the facts of that particular case, the Appellate Division upheld the judgment and order of the High Court Division dismissing the Rule for quashing on the ground that the final report had been submitted on the grounds that there were no disinterested witnesses. The Appellate Division took the view that whether the witnesses who made statements before the police should be relied upon or not is a matter related to the weighing and assessment of evidence and credibility of witnesses, which is the duty of the court trying the case. It may be noted that their Lordships observed that the Indian Supreme Court unanimously decided that there is no bar to entertainment of a second complaint 'in exceptional circumstances'. It was further observed that in that Indian Supreme Court case, viz. Pramatha Nath v. Saroj Ranjan, AIR 1962 SC 876, the majority observed that the second complaint will be entertained "where the previous order was passed on an incomplete record or on a misunderstanding of the nature of the complaint or it was manifestly absurd, unjust or foolish or new fact which could not with reasonable diligence have been brought on the record in the previous proceeding, have been adduced." 

 14. With respect, we agree that there is no bar in law in entertaining a fresh complaint where the accused have been discharged. The bar under section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure after acquittal of an accused does not come into play in the facts of the present case. 

 15. In the case before us, we do not find any exceptional circumstances or discovery of fresh evidence or new facts which would justify entertainment of the second complaint. It cannot be said that the learned Magistrate committed any illegality in the first instance in accepting the police report wherein it had been stated that no independent or material evidence was found to take any legal action. Moreover, the High Court Division has rightly observed that the alleged dispute between the parties, regarding genuineness of a registered sale deed, is of a civil nature.
